header:
How Trader Joe's
keeps prices low

lines.text: Trader Joe's never runs a sale. So how are its prices so low?
lines.say: Trader Joe's never runs a sale. So how are its prices so low?

lines.text: No coupons, no loyalty card. Its website says, "'Sale' is a four-letter word to us."
lines.say: No coupons, no loyalty card either. Its own website says sale is a four-letter word to them.

scene.text: 'Sale' is a four-letter word to us.

lines.text: Secret one: about 80% of what it sells carries the Trader Joe's label.
lines.say: Secret number one. About eighty percent of what it sells carries the Trader Joe's label.

lines.text: Store brands skip the big national ad budgets, and Trader Joe's buys straight from suppliers.
lines.say: Store brands skip the big national ad budgets, and Trader Joe's buys straight from the suppliers.

lines.text: Secret two: it carries only about 4,000 products. Typical supermarkets carry tens of thousands.
lines.say: Secret number two. It carries only about four thousand products, while typical supermarkets carry tens of thousands.

lines.text: Fewer items means bigger orders of each one, and more buying power per product.
lines.say: Fewer items means bigger orders of each one, and more buying power per product.

lines.text: And it's private. Aldi co-founder Theo Albrecht's family has owned it since 1979.
lines.say: And it's private. The family of Aldi co-founder Theo Albrecht has owned it since nineteen seventy-nine.

lines.text: Store brands are booming everywhere: a record $282.8 billion in US sales in 2025.
lines.say: Store brands are booming everywhere, with a record of nearly two hundred eighty-three billion dollars in US sales in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: The takeaway: when a store owns the brand, it controls the price.
lines.say: The takeaway? When a store owns the brand, it controls the price.

post.title: How Trader Joe's keeps prices low with no sales or coupons
post.ig:
Trader Joe's never runs a sale. So how are its prices so low?

About 80% of what it sells carries its own label, and it stocks about 4,000 products instead of tens of thousands.
It buys direct from suppliers and skips national-brand ad budgets.
US store-brand sales hit a record $282.8 billion in 2025 (PLMA/Circana).

Sources: Trader Joe's website FAQ, PLMA/Circana (2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
